    #73565. Industry News: Prediction markets outlook for stocks in 2026 dims amid AI sell-off

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (269 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Prediction markets outlook for stocks in 2026 dims amid AI sell-off

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (269 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • Recent findings suggest that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    It has been revealed that on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note remarked.

    Industry observers note that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    • Another week without Kenneth Walker III?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 11 is underway, and we're tracking all of the injuries before game time.

    AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots (bye) | JetsAFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns (bye) | SteelersAFC South: Texans (played Thurs.) | Colts (played Thurs.) | Jaguars | TitansAFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | ChargersNFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | CommandersNFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers (bye) | VikingsNFC South: Falcons (bye) | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers (bye)NFC West: Cardinals | Rams (bye) | 49ers | Seahawks (bye).

    Another week without Kenneth Walker III? It's looking that way for the Kansas City Chiefs.

    After missing Week 10 due to groin tightness, the Chiefs running back did not practice this week and has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals. Rookie Emmett Johnson, who rushed for 101 yards and caught two receiving touchdowns last week, will once again take on the starter's role.

    On Friday, Reid mentioned Walker, as well as offensive lineman Jaylon Moore and guard Trey Smith, are "improving" as they deal with injuries, but all have been ruled out.

    Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent surgery to repair his MCL this week, head coach Sean McVay unveiled on Friday. The procedure will rule him out for the next few months, which could result in him missing the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

    "We always thought [it] was a possibility," McVay noted regarding Nacua's surgery. "It's going to be a couple months and we're going to have to go on without him.".

    The 6-4 Rams, who are on a bye in Week 11 and play Thanksgiving Eve against the Green Bay Packers, are presently tied for second in the NFC West and have seven more games left in the regular season. McVay did not have a definitive timeline for a return. The team is currently scheduled to play its Week 18 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Jan. 3, a game that could be flexed depending on what the playoff picture looks like at the time.

    McVay did not rule out a Nacua return should the Rams make the postseason, but stated, "you're planning on not having him.".

    Other Week 11 injuries to monitor:.

    Sources indicate that luther Burden III (concussion) has cleared protocol after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit in Week 8 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Chicago Bears wide receiver logged three full practices this week and carries no injury designation. Same goes for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who was limited this week with a knee issue. "Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he mentioned.

    Sources indicate that injuries that kept him limited in Wednesday's practice did not keep Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) away from being on the field Thursday and Friday. The Raiders' leading receiver exited Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks after just 11 snaps with an ankle concern. He is presently listed as questionable.

    Recent findings suggest that the Cardinals will start 40-year-old Josh Johnson against the Chiefs as Carson Beck (beck) has been ruled out. Johnson, who is on his 15th NFL team, is the team's fourth different starter at quarterback in the past four weeks following Beck, Gardner Minshew and Jacoby Brissett.

    DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has missed the past three games for the Philadelphia Eagles, but indicates he's 100% and has felt that way for a while. Smith mentioned he was able to play last week against the Carolina Panthers, but some things are out of his control. He carries no injury designation for Week 11.

    Here's the rest of the Week 11 injury report:.

    Sources indicate that the NHL is not what it is today without Ovechkin and Crosby, and they entered the league together in 2005. They have faced off 100 times in the NHL, including 25 games in the playoffs. In those 100, they have combined for 231 points. A total of 90 games saw either find the score sheet and 49 had both record a point in the same game.

    They have met in four postseason series, each in the second round. Crosby and the Penguins won the first three series and won the Cup each time. Ovechkin has 38 goals and 33 helpers.

    The 39-year-old Crosby is in the final year of his contract but has remarked he has no prepares to retire. He and Ovechkin have joined Howe, Alex Delvecchio, Stan Mikita and Steve Yzerman as the only players in NHL history to play 22 seasons with one franchise.

    According to recent reports, "Over the years, obviously, I've developed a friendship with him and have a ton of respect for him," Crosby said to the media Monday with the Ovechkin news. "It's tough, you come into the league at 18 years old, and before we even met, we were built up against each other.".

    Recent findings suggest that it should be Logan Thompson in net for Washington, and he was excellent in his season debut in allowing two goals in a win at defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina last Friday. Last season at home, he was 19-9-5 with a 2.18 GAA and three shutouts. Thompson made two starts vs. Pittsburgh overall last campaign and won both with a 1.50 GAA.

    The Penguins and Capitals have three meetings left, including Washington's home finale on April 4. That should be quite the Sunday night if both Crosby and Ovechkin are healthy then. Tickets on the secondary market are north of $800 to get in.

    Fresh York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team declared on Saturday.

    Sources indicate that shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    In a recent development, prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    Sources indicate that shesterkin was a significant reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    Sources indicate that dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    Industry observers note that new York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    It has been revealed that new York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    Industry observers note that the one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    According to recent reports, obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and Fresh York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether Upcoming York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of massive swings in recent history.

    #73476. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1291 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1291 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.
    • There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.
    • Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    Since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    Industry observers note that there isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    Industry observers note that he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the major-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a newly introduced procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    It has been revealed that again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

    For those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    Industry observers note that A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    Recent findings suggest that yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    Sources indicate that gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    Sources indicate that stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    According to recent reports, justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    Recent findings suggest that david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    Recent findings suggest that corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    It has been revealed that zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    It has been revealed that max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

    MLB rumors: Phillies OF on the trading block, Blue Jays eye ex-Yankee, plus Mets, Mariners, Braves, Rays, more

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas.
    • Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.
    • We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

    Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

    We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

    Phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

    Industry observers note that the Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

    The Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a substantial bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

    The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

    Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

    The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

    The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

    As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

    Recent findings suggest that marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

    The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

    It has been revealed that happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

    The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

    Yesterday's big news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

    It has been revealed that bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

    Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

    May, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He showed flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

    Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that indicates a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

    Recent findings suggest that jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

    Much has been noted and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

    Recent findings suggest that as we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

    DeLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

    Fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

    "We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to.".

    The Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

    So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

    The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

    The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

    Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a new deal, with injury issues not helping the defender’s case.

    Industry observers note that he told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

    Industry observers note that “His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these challenges stack up eventually.

    “It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a newly introduced contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

    “If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with upcoming players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective newly introduced deals.

    Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

    If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

    As Lewis Steele rightly said, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

    If this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

    Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA unveiled Thursday night.

    According to recent reports, the Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Recent findings suggest that alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).

    The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:.

    Alvarez becomes just the third Astros player to win MVP after Jeff Bagwell in 1994 and Jose Altuve in 2017.

    Rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

    Industry observers note that royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. came in third. This is now his fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.

On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

    #73459. Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1115 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1115 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.
    • Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors.
    • To answer that, we'll look backwards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.

    Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.

    So what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.

    Since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here.

    What road map will PCA's career follow?

    Willie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR.

    For the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year.

    Davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning.

    With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised.

    According to recent reports, césar Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years.

    Sources indicate that it's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons.

    Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson.

    To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old.

    According to recent reports, certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden?

    Then again, few saw it coming with Jones.

    All three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats.".

    Recent findings suggest that through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season.

    Sources indicate that even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh.

    Despite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.

    Mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times.

    Sources indicate that mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23.

    Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3).

    I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine.

    Recent findings suggest that the realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    According to recent reports, not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    It has been revealed that our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Recent findings suggest that steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    In a recent development, finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves.
    • It has been revealed that otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves. Phillips, our 34th-ranked free agent, received a three-year deal worth $35 million. He'll replace Raisel Iglesias in Atlanta's bullpen and pair with Robert Suarez at the end of the game. The Braves could still re-sign Iglesias too, I suppose.

    It has been revealed that otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

    Recent findings suggest that the Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers, though he does not stand out defensively, and could land at first base or in the corner outfield in MLB. Texas could stand to upgrade at first base and could always slot Sato in at DH as well.

    It has been revealed that we ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available and the best free agent position player. The reigning Triple Crown winner in Japan hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. Sato, 28 in March, has some similarities to Munetaka Murakami as a lefty with big power and swing-and-miss concerns, though Sato is a much more aggressive hitter and won't walk as much as Murakami.

    According to recent reports, with Miguel Rojas retired, the Dodgers are looking to add a right-handed hitting infielder, according to The Athletic. Mookie Betts and Max Muncy are entrenched on the left side of the infield. Tommy Edman, a switch-hitter, is penciled in at second base, with fellow switch-hitter Alex Freeland next in line as depth. Freeland has not hit much in his limited MLB time, however.

    According to recent reports, this is not a great free agent class overall, but it does feature several utility infielders who hit right-handed. Among them are Mauricio Dubón, Ha-Seong Kim, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Edmundo Sosa. Glovemen Oswald Peraza (Angels) and Jared Triolo (Pirates) are potential trade targets. Rojas was a very productive role player for Los Angeles. He won't be so easy to replace.

    The Padres are receiving calls about catchers Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Top prospect Ethan Salas was called up in September and became the youngest catcher to appear in the postseason in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Salas is the future behind the plate, making Campusano or Fermin (or perhaps both) expendable.

    Campusano and Fermin are very different players. Campusano is a bat-first catcher who might be worth keeping given his age (28) and the fact that the Padres could slot him at DH. That said, those same qualities make him appealing to other teams. Fermin, 31, is a terrific defender who hasn't hit much the last few years. The Padres need pitching and could deal a catcher or two for an arm or two.

    Samsung Lions outfielder Ja-Wook Koo has hired a latest agent and is looking to make the jump to MLB, reports MLB.com. Koo, a 10-time All-Star and this year's Korean Series MVP, has been among the best hitters in the Korea Baseball Organization the last few years. The 33-year-old hit .371/.458/.581 with 15 homers and nearly as many walks (66) as strikeouts (71) in 2026.

    Koo's age and the fact he's a left-handed hitter in a market inundated with left-handed hitting outfielders will work against him in free agency. He has a great track record in Korea, though, including a history of high contact rates, which could make him a cheaper and more appealing target than MLB free agents like Michael Conforto, Trent Grisham, Cedric Mullins, and Daulton Varsho.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m.
    • Industry observers note that skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly.
    • Something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

    Industry observers note that skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:.

    1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    Recent findings suggest that 2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    Industry observers note that 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several significant-market clubs are said to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

    According to recent reports, there is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN says Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

    It has been revealed that with that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a new contract to stay with his team.

    1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

    Recent findings suggest that 2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a latest salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

    According to recent reports, 3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

    In a recent development, 1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the substantial picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

    2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

    Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander has issued a statement regarding his recent anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted. Santander's statement, which he posted to Instagram and follows a public condemnation of the posts by Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins, reads as follows:.

    "After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform.

    "I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize. I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared, recognizing the responsibility that comes with having a public voice.

    "As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs. After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions.

    "I would like to affirm my respect for the Muslim community and for the dignity and freedom of people of every faith and background.

    "From this experience, I have learned to ensure that none of my communications promote hate or give the impression that I support hatred, discrimination, or violence against anyone.".

    The club had earlier released a statement on the incident that read:.

    "Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs.".

    In a recent development, santander, a Venezuela native, shared social media videos following the recent U.S. midterm elections, including one in which a Christian pastor noted, "There is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another suggested that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate representing the state of Michigan.

    Atkins told reporters Tuesday that Santander's behavior "did not align" with organizational values and there were no words "to express my level of disappointment.".

    Sources indicate that "I talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant," Atkins stated. "We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that.".

    It has been revealed that santander, 32, joined the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season on a five-year, $92.5 million free-agent contract. He struggled badly across 54 games in 2025 and missed the entire 2026 season with injury.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers.
    • Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds.
    • Rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers.

    Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds.

    Rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129. After a timeout, LeBron James threw an inbounds pass to Embiid, who attempted to dribble out the clock near the Milwaukee basket. Embiid stepped out of bounds at the baseline with his left foot, but the officials did not call the turnover and Herro was forced to foul.

    The Bucks could not challenge the non-call because they were out of replay challenges.

    Embiid made his two free throws to put Philadelphia ahead by 3, but the Bucks still had 1.5 seconds remaining to try for a tying basket.

    Sources indicate that herro received the inbounds pass from Kyle Kuzma at the top of the arc and took one dribble to break free from VJ Edgecombe. Shooting from the right elbow, Herro's 3-pointer went in. However, the shot left his hand after the buzzer.

    In a recent development, the eighth-year guard shot 15 for 23 from the floor, including 7 of 13 on 3-pointers. Herro also hit all 11 of his free throws, adding 11 rebounds and seven assists. Burries finished with 26 points off the bench with 8 rebounds and four assists. Kuzma was the third Bucks player to reach double figures, scoring 12 with five boards.

    Herro's previous career-high was 41 points, reached in a December 2022 win over the Houston Rockets while he was with the Miami Heat.

    Milwaukee lost its 13th consecutive game to drop to 1-16 on the season, the worst mark in the NBA. The Bucks' only win came nearly a month ago on Oct. 26, a 110-102 victory over the Indiana Pacers. Up next for them is the Toronto Raptors (6-10) at home on Monday.

    Embiid led the Sixers with 26 points, nearly registering a triple-double with 17 rebounds and nine assists. James added 21 points with 6 boards, 6 assists and 3 steals. Seven Philadelphia players scored in double figures, with Anfernee Simons getting 18 off the bench and Tyrese Maxey tallying 17 points.

    The 76ers improved to 14-3 with the win, tying the Los Angeles Lakers for the NBA's top record. Philadelphia has won five consecutive games and next faces the Portland Trail Blazers (10-5) on Monday.

    • The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions.
    • Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason.
    • According to recent reports, the Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

    According to recent reports, the Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

    Sources indicate that the Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

    It has been revealed that the Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the significant leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

    That said, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

    In a recent development, not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

    Industry observers note that the Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

    According to recent reports, the Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

    Industry observers note that we ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

    According to recent reports, the Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

    Industry observers note that schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

    Sources indicate that the Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

    The Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

    According to recent reports, the Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

    Recent findings suggest that leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings.
    • 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place?
    • For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

    With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

    For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

    Sources indicate that tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a significant-league game in 2026, is at the moment on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

    Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

    According to recent reports, boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

    "I'm not going to speak to that right now," he mentioned "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of.".

    Now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

    In a recent development, because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

    Hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

    None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

    The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

    "He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright significant-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field.".

    Sources indicate that the Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

    Bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

    It has been revealed that with Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

    In a recent development, one is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

    Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

    Naturally, there is some apprehension.

    Sources indicate that "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow said. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Sources indicate that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • In a recent development, hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Newly introduced Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams revealed the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He stated at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    In a recent development, hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    Recent findings suggest that after trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Fresh Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a latest era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    According to recent reports, goaltending has been an matter in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Sources indicate that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    It has been revealed that in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In a recent development, in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    In a recent development, the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Recent findings suggest that although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    According to recent reports, if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    In a recent development, let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    Recent findings suggest that with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his newly introduced team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    #73435. 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year
